svg.title: Address reuse and stale handle identity
svg.desc: Slot zero is first owned by request R attempt one at generation seven. After readers finish and one safe return, it is reused at the same symbolic address by T attempt one at generation eight. The old handle must reject; validation also needs protected lifetime.
svg.text: Same location does not mean the same request state
Symbolic pool: 2 slots × 64 KiB = 128 KiB backing payload
Before retirement: slot 0, address A0, generation 7
Owner: request R / attempt 1; teaching handle: (0, 7)
Slot 1 belongs to request S / attempt 1 and remains separate.
Close new use → wait for readers → return once
Existing storage stays live until the lifetime conditions hold.
After reuse: slot 0, address A0, generation 8
Owner: request T / attempt 1; current handle: (0, 8)
Old handle (0, 7) must reject despite the repeated address.
Generation, owner, attempt, layer, prefix, state and bounds are separate checks.
A validated lookup also needs a lifetime guard against concurrent reclamation.
